sources.title: Current consolidated Question projection for both compare-version source rows
Tagged interview source containing Compare Version Numbers prompt

claims.text: Both current source Questions ask the same standalone compare-version-numbers operation; detailed parsing and malformed-input rules are not preserved source facts.

The candidate explicitly adopts dot-separated nonnegative decimal revisions, ignores leading zeros, treats missing trailing revisions as zero, and rejects malformed/non-decimal input as an answer-side executable boundary.

Writer and independent reviewer validations verify trailing-zero equality, leading-zero equality, first-difference ordering, arbitrary-length revision comparison and explicit rejection outside the adopted contract.

validation.command: extract exact candidate Java block; javac; execute independent adversarial reviewer harness
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact-candidate trailing-zero leading-zero first-difference arbitrary-length malformed-input contract-boundary
checks: exact candidate Java implementation compiles under Java 21
missing trailing revisions compare as zero under the explicitly adopted answer-side contract
leading-zero revisions compare numerically and first differing revision determines ordering
arbitrary-length decimal revisions compare without finite-width integer overflow
empty, malformed, signed, prerelease-like and null inputs are explicitly rejected outside the adopted contract

findings: The two current repository Questions preserve the same standalone compare-version-numbers operation; neither preserves a complete parsing, malformed-input, numeric-width, or SemVer contract.
The candidate labels its dot-separated nonnegative-decimal revision rules as an answer-side executable contract rather than source facts.
The exact Java code compiles and independently passes trailing-zero equality, leading-zero equality, first-difference ordering, arbitrary-length revision and malformed-input checks.
Length-then-lexicographic comparison after removing leading zeros is correct for nonnegative decimal revisions and avoids an unstated int/long width limit.
The answer explicitly excludes signed/prerelease-like inputs and states that it is not a SemVer comparator; no fabricated production experience is claimed.
